#1408. Ferrero sets Juventus ambition to be what it once was, as €200m capital raise runs

Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero set out the leadership's view of the rebuild at the Brussels launch of the club's European Union fan club. He spoke while a capital raise of about €200m is open and a UEFA settlement limits spending.

Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero went to Brussels on 18 November with a clear message for supporters. Restoring the club to its former self is its absolute ambition, he said, adding that the club is following the path set out by its chief executive and is confident this can happen. He spoke at the opening of the Juventus Official Fan Club European Union, which is chaired by MEP Sandro Gozi. The timing gives the statement weight.

The new supporters’ club opened at the Iosono il Piemonte event space. Its stated purpose is to link Juventus supporters with the institutional centre of Europe.

Before the opening, the delegation went to the European Parliament with Gozi. Chief Club Affairs Officer Giorgio Chiellini led the group alongside Ferrero. Piedmont regional president Alberto Cirio attended the opening, as did MEPs who have joined the fan club.

The visit showed Chiellini’s work on the club’s relations with institutions and European football. It also gives supporters an official club in Brussels.

The financial backdrop is demanding. Juventus posted a consolidated loss of €66m for 2025/26. On 12 November, the board approved the offer, using part of the €250m authority granted by shareholders at the extraordinary meeting on 3 November.

The offer involves up to 208.5m new shares at €0.96 each. Shareholders can buy one new share for every two they hold. The price is 28.36% below the theoretical ex-rights price, based on that day’s share price. The remaining €50m of the authority can be used in later financial years, depending on the club’s financial needs and investment plans.

The spending limits come from UEFA. European football’s governing body fined Juventus €20m for breaking the football earnings rule. Of that amount, €14m is conditional. The club agreed a three-year settlement with annual targets. It also faces limits on registering new players on its UEFA List A.

Those are the limits within which Ferrero’s ambition must be pursued. Any improvement in the squad has to fit within the annual targets agreed with UEFA.

Subscription rights can be traded on Euronext Milan until 25 November, and the offer closes on 1 December 2026.

#1407. Bayern Munich announces several months of absence for Harry Kane!

Bayern Munich will have to face a very big blow. Hit in the left ankle during the match against Cologne (1-1), Friday evening, Harry Kane (33) suffers from a rupture of the syndesmotic ligament, as officially announced by the Bavarian club. The diagnosis was confirmed by the medical service after examinations. At 33, the English striker is preparing to miss an important period of the season, a real blow for Vincent Kompany and the reigning Ballon d’Or.

The Three Lions scorer was forced to leave his partners in the 20th minute after contact with Joël Schmied. A premature exit which quickly aroused the concern of the Munich staff. While the first information already suggested a serious injury, the Bayern press release confirmed fears: Kane will be absent “over the next few months”. A duration which could notably deprive him of several important meetings with the German champion.

An absence which could notably deprive Bayern of its scorer during several important European matches, starting with the trip to Lille, on November 25, and the reception of Slavia Prague, on December 8. This injury also adds to the already busy Bavarian infirmary. Before this meeting, Bayern had to deal without Manuel Neuer, Serge Gnabry, Ismaël Saibari, Alphonso Davies and Luis Díaz. Michael Olise also left the field at half-time against Cologne.

The French international, however, suffers from“a bruise on the forefoot and will be treated in the coming days”according to the Recorder’s press release. For Vincent Kompany, the loss of his main offensive asset therefore represents a serious headache as an important period in the calendar approaches. Bayern will have to quickly find solutions to compensate for their striker’s loss with a view to their next European matches, including the meeting against LOSC.

#1406. Kean’s new tibia injury rules former Juventus striker out of Como v Juventus

Moise Kean has broken down again in Como training, three weeks after treatment that was meant to fix his shin. The former Juventus striker is set to miss about two more months, so he will not face his old club on 29 November.

Moise Kean has suffered a new tibia injury in training with Como. The former Juventus striker is now undergoing further medical tests. Sky Sport Italia reported that he will be out for about two more months. That timeline rules him out of Como’s home game against Juventus.

Como’s statement of 17 November gave no recovery date. The club promised an update once more information was available.

The new problem follows a treatment that was meant to end his shin trouble. On 30 October, Como’s update described his treatment at the Cugat Institute in Barcelona as successful. The club put his recovery at about five weeks. His progress was to be reviewed every day.

That plan has now collapsed. Kean had been out since early October. The original injury came while he was playing for Italy against France on 2 October. That match was the first leg of a Nations League tie.

The setback is a heavy blow for Como. In Serie A, his outings for the club added up to 160 minutes. He has yet to score, including in his single Champions League game. He joined from Fiorentina on an initial loan, with an obligation to make the move permanent. At Fiorentina he scored 27 league goals in two seasons, 19 of them in 2024/25. Before that, he came through the Juventus academy.

Without him, Como will have to rely on Douvikas up front. The club may also look for a striker in January.

For Juventus, the news removes one threat from a crucial stretch. Como are their next opponents after Venezia. The game is the Sunday evening fixture a week later, in round 13 of Serie A. Kick-off is at 20:45.

Como 1907 is pleased to announce the signing of Italian international forward Moise Kean from @acffiorentina on an initial loan, with an obligation to make the move permanent.

Official statement ➡️ https://t.co/PJKnFXS9Xp pic.twitter.com/4F30ROYFUT

— Como1907 (@Como_1907) September 1, 2026

Luciano Spalletti’s side need results. Juventus sit six points behind fourth place and have averaged just over 1.6 points per game, according to Corriere dello Sport. The paper sees the run of fixtures as decisive for the push for a Champions League place. It warns that dropping points against Venezia would force Juventus to win every remaining game of 2026 to stay in touch with the top four.

The schedule offers little respite after the trip to Como. Juventus host Udinese on 6 December and Monza on 14 December. They then travel to Roma on 19 December.

#1403. Como beat Cagliari 2-0 to go back into fourth, eight points clear of next opponents Juventus

Como beat Cagliari 2-0 with two headers from Yan Couto crosses, moving back into fourth place on 26 points. Juventus visit next and trail the side holding the last Champions League place by eight points.

Como beat Cagliari 2-0 at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia on Saturday, 21 November 2026. Both goals were headers, and Yan Couto crossed for both of them. The result lifted Fàbregas’ side back into fourth place. That is the last Champions League place, and Juventus are the next visitors.

Ramón opened the scoring after 24 minutes. He met Couto’s cross from the right and headed past goalkeeper Caprile. Da Cunha, the captain, doubled the lead in the 56th minute. He headed in another Couto delivery from the centre of the area.

Fàbregas left Nico Paz and Perrone on the bench. The two Argentinians had rejoined the squad only hours before kick-off after international duty. Como play AEK in the Champions League on Tuesday. Even without the pair from the start, the hosts kept Cagliari out. Both men entered in the 57th minute, with Liberali and Milla making way respectively. It was Como’s first win since a defeat to Inter before the international break.

For Fàbregas, the performance was not perfect, but he was very pleased. Perrone had a minor problem, the coach explained, which ruled out a full 90 minutes for the midfielder.

Como have now won three Serie A home games in a row without conceding, which they last did in October and November 1984, according to Sportmediaset. Da Cunha has three goals in his last four games across Serie A and the Champions League. Fàbregas has never lost to Cagliari in five Serie A matches as a coach. He has won three of them and drawn two. Cagliari have lost each of their last four away league games. That is their first run of four straight away defeats in Serie A since November–December 2023.

Como have eight wins, two draws and two defeats from 12 games, according to Como 1907. They have scored 20 goals and conceded 10.

In that table, Juventus’ record reads five wins, three draws and three defeats. They have scored 15 goals and conceded 12. The gap to Como stood at eight points before Juventus’ game against Venezia.

Il @Como_1907 in chiusura per Yan Couto: operazione in prestito con diritto di riscatto. @SkySport https://t.co/6208TSUvqL

— Gianluca Di Marzio (@DiMarzio) July 7, 2026

Juventus have played one game fewer. Even so, Como have scored more and conceded fewer. Juventus will face a side whose crossing from the right produced both goals on Saturday.

Como face AEK first. After that European tie, attention turns to the visit of Juventus. The Bianconeri travel to the Sinigaglia on Sunday 29 November, with kick-off set for 20:45 CET.

#1402. Endrick threatens Real Madrid with January departure

While FC Barcelona fears every minute played by Raphinha with the Brazil jersey, Real Madrid has the opposite position: they want Endrick to play as much as possible with their selection. Obviously, this is linked to the status of the young Brazilian within Casa Blaca, where he has to make do with crumbs. Since the last break, Endrick has benefited from 136 minutes of playing time at Real, compared to 139 during the 3 matches played with Brazil, which means he needs his selection to stretch his legs.

Endrick therefore joined his selection, which will face Japan then Singapore during this break, with the ambition of playing as much as possible, which will allow him to show himself, in the eyes of his coach José Mourinho, but also of the clubs interested in his services. Because it is one of the major issues for Real during the next winter transfer window, since Mourinho has already declared that he wants to keep him. “He’s a player that I adore, a player that I love deeply. He has great potential and he is very important for us. Anyone interested in Endrick will have to fight me. I don’t think he needs to be loaned out; he will do very well here”he said.

But does Endrick have the same opinion? He spoke about his future during a short mixed zone upon his arrival at the Brazilian rally. “I don’t know what will happen in January. It’s in God’s hands. I only ask what is best for my career. Come what may. I will keep my feet on the ground and do my best. Madrid is a beautiful city, but I will always do everything possible to advance my career”he explained, making it clear that a departure was possible on his side, even if he will not take unnecessary risks.

“I am still very young. I don’t need to throw myself headlong into the void. I’m only 20 and we’ll see. I just want to play, be happy, help my teammates… Score goals, make assists, like I did in Lyon, which remains one of the best experiences of my life and one of the happiest moments of my existence.”he recalled, he who is under contract until 2030. His time in Lyon had left him with good memories, and vice versa. It remains to be seen whether by January, he will have skyrocketed his playing time at Real Madrid.

#1401. Inter throw away three two-goal leads at Atalanta as Juventus stay eight points back

Inter drew 4-4 at Bergamo after leading 2-0, 3-1 and 4-2, and dropped to third behind Lazio and Roma. Juventus sit eight points behind them before Thursday's Europa League game with Omonia and Sunday's trip to Como.

Inter led 2-0, then 3-1, then 4-2 at the New Balance Arena on Sunday night. They still left Bergamo with a single point. The 4-4 draw with Atalanta left Chivu’s side third, three points behind leaders Lazio on 32 and now overtaken by Roma on 30.

Behind them, Milan have 27 and Como 26. Inter’s advantage over Juventus stands at eight points. The top of the table is spreading out, and Inter’s slip leaves three clubs within three points of each other at the summit.

Esposito gave Inter a two-goal cushion with his first two goals of the night. Elmas pulled one back for Atalanta on 35 minutes. Esposito restored the margin seven minutes after half-time to complete his hat-trick.

Atalanta played with a late change in goal. Sportiello started because Carnesecchi had to pull out during the warm-up. De Ketelaere cut the gap on 72 minutes. Four minutes later Zappacosta handled a Thuram shot on the goal line. Inter’s advantage was back to two goals once Sučić beat Sportiello with the resulting penalty.

De Ketelaere struck for a second time on 81 minutes. Bastoni’s handball then gave Atalanta a stoppage-time penalty, and Kessié converted it.

Chivu said his side had failed the exam in the final minutes. He called the result “two gifted points”. Esposito now has six goals this season, and no Inter player has scored more in Serie A.

Inter also lost Hakan Çalhanoğlu. He came off in the 33rd minute with a problem in the hamstring of his right thigh and is due to have tests on Tuesday 24 November, Sky Sport reported. He will miss Wednesday’s Champions League game against Stuttgart and Saturday’s league match with Genoa at San Siro. It is his second muscle injury of the season, after a layoff of about 20 days in September.

Juventus arrive at their own busy week in form. All four goals against Venezia came after half-time, from Woltemade, Koopmeiners, Cabal and a Kolo Muani penalty. The win came in Luciano Spalletti’s 600th Serie A game as a coach.

The Europa League comes first. Kick-off for Thursday’s league-phase meeting at the Allianz Stadium is at 21:00. Three days later they visit Como, one of the clubs above them, in round 13 on Sunday 29 November 2026 at 20:45.

The direct test against Inter is further away. The league meeting between the two clubs is set for Sunday 10 January 2027 at 20:45.

#1400. MU: Mauricio Pochettino could delay his arrival

Manchester United will have to wait before being able to count on Mauricio Pochettino. While an agreement has reportedly been reached to make the United States coach the successor to Michael Carrick, the Argentine coach is not expected to immediately join the Red Devils. According to information from The AthleticPochettino would have decided to finish the international gathering with the American selection before taking up his new role at Old Trafford. A situation which could complicate the debut of the 54-year-old technician, since Manchester United hoped to take advantage of this truce to prepare for his arrival and allow him to work with his new squad. Mancunian leaders would nevertheless have accepted this schedule, while a financial agreement estimated at 9 million euros would have been found with the American Federation to release the former coach of Tottenham and PSG.

Despite the numerous information regarding his future, Mauricio Pochettino continues to behave normally with his players. When training resumed with the United States, the Argentinian only mentioned the session program and the integration of three young players from the under-20s, without referring to Manchester United. “ Everything here is as usual. We practice and play like we don’t hear anything “, explained American defender Chris Richards, recognizing however that the group had become aware of the rumors. “ We train like he’s going to be our coach again tomorrow, because we don’t know what’s going to happen “, he added. The United States is scheduled to face Haiti twice in the CONCACAF Nations League, Saturday in Miami and Tuesday in Cincinnati. An immediate departure of Pochettino and his deputy Jesús Pérez would therefore place the American Federation in a delicate situation. For Manchester United, this setback could have sporting consequences: if his appointment is confirmed, the Argentinian would only have a few days to prepare for his first match, scheduled for Liverpool.

#1399. Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

This particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

So to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

“I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba said. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”

Floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

As impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy

“It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca said. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”

Allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has said supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was important for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca said.

Cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

All told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

With the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:

Erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

Great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

Mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

Samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

Big cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

What a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

And Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

Maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:

And without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

Credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

As we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

Samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

And the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

Samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

He has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

Norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic shows some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

Kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

Spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

Khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

Norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

It’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off here are the teams for tonight’s fixture:

Man City XI: Rulli; O’Reilly, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Lewis; Kovacic (c), Bouaddi; Ait-Nouri, Cherki, Allan; Samba

Subs: Anderson, Braithwaite, Donnarumma, Fernández, Guéhi, McAidoo, Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes, Semenyo

Norwich City XI: Grimshaw; Yongwa, Bruno Alves, Darling (c), Fisher; Field, Wright; Diallo, Ben Slimane, Crnac; Kvistgaarden

Subs: Chrisene, Mattsson, Kovacevic, Maghoma, McConville, Musaba, Schwartau, Stacey, Touré

"It's part of the decision that I took when I decided to join this club"Enzo Maresca responds to the doubts surrounding him filling Pep Guardiola's shoes 👇 pic.twitter.com/o6eUjQUOnU

David 🆚 Goliath 🤝🎥 https://t.co/5YXw2tQvfX pic.twitter.com/fTp9zD0xiX

As Abdukodir Khusanov makes his fourth start of the season, Hugo Viana, Man City director of football, has been speaking about the young Uzbek. The 22-year-old signed a new five-year contract with City in July, and Viana has affirmed that he “will be one of the best centre-backs in the world”.

"Abdukodir Khusanov will be one of the best centre-backs in the world" - Hugo Viana 🇺🇿🌏Full interview 🔗 https://t.co/dk3Qi8DF8D pic.twitter.com/hHdVdX5HSF

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

Speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

Keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

His older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

City fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

Checking in 🚌🚶‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/xWYGyaH7TY

Ⓒ Darling with the armband🧤 Grimshaw in goal⚡️ Ante on the rightYour Yellows for this evening ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/znOGtvyJyk

Your City side to take on Norwich 👊XI | Rulli, Lewis, Khusanov, Reis, O'Reilly, Bouaddi, Kovačić (C), Samba, Allan, Aït-Nouri, CherkiSUBS | Donnarumma, Anderson, Guéhi, Ndiaye, Fernández, Nunes, Semenyo, McAidoo, Braithwaite🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/LCA4WfACBf

Good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

These two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

Philippe Clement’s side beat MK Dons 4-1 in the first round, and followed that up with a 2-1 win over Cardiff City in the second to reach the Etihad tonight. The fourth-round draw has already been done, and it has been decided that the winner of this match will face Brighton.

But we have at least 90 minutes of the third round left before that, so without further ado, we’ll get underway and bring you team updates shortly!

#1398. Nations League: first defeat for Zinédine Zidane’s Blues against a stunning Italy

A return to basics for Zinédine Zidane’s 5th match at the head of the France team, in a San Siro stadium which saw his debut as a player for Juventus Turin thirty years ago. But it was above all the desire to continue the work started during an attractive first gathering that motivated Zizou for this Italy-France, 5th day of the Nations League. Faced with an opponent who had drawn the match at the Stade de France, the Blues started the match very well, despite constant rain and a pitch in a deplorable state. With Barcola positioned at number 9 and a Da Cunha-Rabiot-Cherki trio in the midfield, they stifled the pale Italians and created the first chances.

Donnarumma worked on a header from Rabiot, from close range (9th), before sinking by sending a restart, at the foot, directly into those of Michael Olise, who took great pleasure in eliminating Bastoni before adjusting Donnarumma (0-1, 11th). Thanks to another very interesting pressing, Zidane’s men did not leave much to their hosts, who still ideally exploited a rare opportunity. Cambiaghi overwhelmed Gusto and crossed hard at the near post for Pio Esposito, more lively than the French defense to deceive Maignan (1-1, 26th). Which had the gift of waking up the players of Mancini and San Siro.

Barcola found the post, in the 35th minute, with a beautiful curling shot, but the French team returned to the locker room with the score 1-1. Returning from the locker room, Malo Gusto won his first duel of the evening against Cambiaghi but came close to being penalized for a shirt pulling in his area. The Blues accelerated again and, thanks to their pressing, offered themselves a superb opportunity which Cherki wasted by refusing to shoot quickly (51st). The French midfielder started in the 52nd minute, but the right post repelled his attempt. Rabiot once again came up against Donnarumma (58th), before Gusto did the irreparable by irregularly stopping the very restless Cambiaghi in the area (58th). Fortunately, Sebastiano Esposito sent a shot off target (60th).

The match was going completely crazy, Roberto Mancini took out Cambiaghi but his replacement Dimarco was decisive with a cross for Frattesi, who beat Jacquet to shoot Maignan (2-1, 63rd). And the French team, far from being sovereign on the defensive level, which again made mistakes. Truffert took too big a risk on a restart, Vergara appeared, pushing Upamecano to make a mistake. This time, it was Pio Esposito who took charge of the penalty and he made no mistake (3-1, 75th). Zidane then changed his two full-backs, with the entries of Diouf and Kumbedi, and launched Kroupi and Mayulu in place of Barcola and Doué. Then Camavinga replaced Cherki but that changed nothing in the scenario of the meeting. Already frustrated by Italy at the Stade de France, Zinedine Zidane experienced his first defeat against Squadra Azzurra, which even went ahead of France in the group 1 standings.

#1396. Roberto De Zerbi defends Mykhailo Mudryk after on-loan star angered Spurs fans with interview gaffes - including admitting he wanted to join Arsenal

Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:35 EST, 20 November 2026

Mykhailo Mudryk is still two weeks away from a Tottenham return after a suffering setback to his recovery from an ankle injury.

Mudryk, who has played only 16 minutes since joining on loan from Chelsea, clashed with the Ukrainian FA this week when he blamed them for his positive drug test which ruled him out of football for almost two years.

He also risked the wrath of Spurs fans by admitting he only made the move across London to recover his fitness before returning to Stamford Bridge where Blues boss Xabi Alonso was 'counting on him'.

And he managed to annoy both Chelsea and Spurs fans by revealing, during the same YouTube interview, that he wanted to sign for Arsenal when he moved to the Premier League in January 2023 but his agent forced through the move with the best commission.

'I can understand the fans, but Mudryk is a good guy,' said Spurs boss De Zerbi, who worked with the Ukraine international at Shakhtar Dontetsk and convinced him to resist interest from Brentford and Coventry and be reunited in North London.

'He's a good player. He suffered a lot for the situation in the last couple of years. He has just one thing to do, show on the pitch his qualities, show on the pitch that now he's playing for Tottenham. Tottenham is a big club, like the other clubs, not less at all.'

Mykhailo Mudryk admitted he joined Tottenham to regain fitness before returning to Chelsea, while also stating he had wanted to sign for Arsenal in 2023 before his transfer to the Blues

Roberto De Zerbi acknowledged Tottenham fans' views on Mudryk's comments, but insisted the winger has 'suffered a lot' following his doping ban

Chelsea paid £86million for Mudryk but he made little impression before he was hit with a four-year ban in 2024, which was wiped out this summer enabling him to return to competition.

'He has no responsibility in this part,' said De Zerbi. 'Now his focus is just on the ball or just on the football. He has a big chance to play with us because Tottenham is a big club. He knows very well the coach, he knows very well the style of play.

'He knows I give him total confidence to show what he is. So to move the focus in the right direction, in a good direction. But I think he's working hard to recover and to play earlier.'

Mudryk made his Spurs debut as a sub at Nottingham Forest in September but injured an ankle in training a few days later. He was initially expected to be out for two months with Saturday's game against Ipswich his target to return.

'The plan was to be available for Ipswich or Sunderland,' said De Zerbi, who will serve a touchline ban against Ipswich for three yellow cards. 'Then he felt not pain but he was not comfortable last week. And they take two weeks more, and step by step we're going to see the situation.'

James Maddison's limited involvement for Tottenham relates to a niggling hip injury dating back to pre-season.

Maddison has been an unused sub in two Spurs games since limping off when the problem flared up at Chelsea, on his second start of the season and his second start in six days.

Roberto De Zerbi confirmed ahead of Saturday's game against Ipswich that it had been the same problem which dogged Maddison through the summer as he fought back from a serious knee injury.

The Spurs boss revealed how his physical condition had suffered from not training regularly and reminded the 29-year-old England midfielder he could only make an impact in the Premier League in peak condition.

De Zerbi confirmed James Maddison is available to face Ipswich but stressed the midfielder needs to push himself to reach his peak physical condition

'It is not a big injury, but he was not able to work,' explained De Zerbi. 'He had a problem with his hip. The same as preseason. It's not a big problem but if you don't work consistently you lose the physical condition and to play in this level of competition you have to stay in the top physical condition.'

Maddison, who turns 30 on Monday, missed most of last season with a cruciate knee injury and has played only 195 minutes this season. His return was further complicated by a shoulder injury after coming on at Brentford on the opening game of the season.

'He is still young, 29 years is not old,' said De Zerbi. 'He has to push and demand of himself the top in terms of physical condition, because if he is 80 or 90 per cent of his physical condition he makes the difference for us, he changes the games.'

Maddison and Destiny Udogie have both trained fully through the international break and are available to face Ipswich.

'He worked very well from the Wednesday after Leeds,' said De Zerbi. 'From Chelsea to the Leeds game, he worked just three times on the pitch at the training ground.

'If you don't work during the week you risk injury and lose the normal physical condition you need to play Premier League. The same for Udogie. When they work and are fit to work, they have many chances to play, especially Maddison because a special player.'

Maddison's first start of the season came against Coventry when he scored the opener and inspired Spurs to their first win. He barely trained but started again in the win at Chelsea five days later, where he broke down early in the second half and was replaced by Conor Gallagher.

De Zerbi made it clear there were no problems connected to Maddison being pictured out at a pub in Coventry after the defeat at Leeds. It was the last game before the international break and the first of three days off.

'I am angry because next time he has to invite me,' joked the Spurs boss and he added: 'I am happy. I know when my players work well. If they are serious on the pitch, off the pitch they can do what they want. I'm not a policeman.

'James is top professional, top guy, top player. The private life is not our problem if they work well and they are serious, and give their best for the club, the shirt and the fans, and he is perfect when it comes to that.'

#1394. Senegal-Morocco: CAS verdict, Romain Molina makes a major announcement

The soap opera surrounding the controversial CAN 2025 final between Senegal and Morocco will soon reach its epilogue. This Monday, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) announced through a press release that its verdict will be revealed this Tuesday afternoon, ten months after the meeting.

Since this CAS announcement, speculation and false information have been rife on social networks. This is why Romain Molina wanted to warn against the many rumors currently circulating.

“Anything that can currently circulate on the networks must not be taken into account”wrote the independent journalist on his X account. A message intended to calm speculation as the wait around this affair continues to grow.

As a reminder, the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) contacted the CAS after the decision of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) to award a victory on the green carpet to Morocco (3-0). The Senegalese contest this decision, taken after the incidents that occurred during the final, initially won on the field (1-0 after) by the Lions of Teranga.

#1393. Dovbyk open to joining Valencia in January

Artem Dovbyk’s time at Bologna is set to end in January.

The Ukrainian isn’t part of Raffaele Palladino’s plans, and Roma has no intention of seeing the striker lose value.

A return to Spain is one of the most likely options for the 1997-born striker, but several factors need to be considered.

A Spanish club has reportedly shown interest in the striker from the Roman club.

Valencia is reportedly open to a loan move if the striker were to return to Trigoria early. And the first hurdle—the player’s desire—seems to have been overcome.

According to reports from Spain, Cadena SER, Dovbyk has opened his eyes to Valencia. The player is reportedly happy to return to Spain, where he excelled and convinced Roma to shell out millions to bring him to Trigoria.

The striker has instructed his agents to find a solution to make the transfer a reality. The Pipistrelli are unable to meet the Trigoria club’s financial demands and can only offer a loan with an option to buy.

The ball is now in the clubs’ court, who want to find a solution to close the deal. The Spanish club is expected to pay €1.5 million to the Roman club and 50% of the player’s salary, following the terms established for the 1997-born player’s transfer to Bologna.

The Giallorossi paid €35 ​​million plus bonuses for the Ukrainian, and are currently struggling to find buyers.

#1392. Bayern Munich can’t stand Jamal Musiala’s situation any longer!

Bayern Munich had a very difficult evening when they received Cologne (1-1). Harry Kane came off with a serious ankle injury after 20 minutes. At the break, it was Michael Olise who had to give up his place, also affected, less severely, but he still left the stadium on crutches. For the Frenchman, we do not yet know his length of unavailability but it should not be too long, compared to the Ballon d’Or. The Englishman will have to be absent for several months after rupturing an ankle ligament.

Jamal Musiala played the last 20 minutes of the game. He is still facing health problems, he who suffers from a neurological dysfunction preventing him from being able to last the length of a match. Problem, he is one of the highest paid players at the club and his situation is starting to get talked about. Until then, he had always received the full support of his management but the first flaws appeared last night with a vitriolic interview with Karl-Heinz Rummenigge. The latter let go a little about the future of the 23-year-old player.

To summarize, the Bavarian legend considers that this situation is no longer tenable. “It’s entirely possible (that he regains his level, editor’s note) and we cannot rule it out. Unfortunately, what we know suggests that it will be difficult to reach the level he has so often displayed here.immediately hits the member of the supervisory board, and former chairman of the club’s board of directors, before continuing. “We need to talk to the family, the player and especially his representatives. These sums are no longer possible – sorry, with all due respect.»

The former striker continues his explanation by highlighting the interests of the club. “I can’t imagine Jamal leaving the club or another club buying him in these circumstances. This is problematic. We handled the situation very tactfully with the player, and we all want him back, ideally at the top of his form. But what will happen if this is not the case?he asks. It will then be necessary to look at the financial aspects. And this is a task that unfortunately falls to the board of directors and the supervisory board.»

A meeting will soon take place, Rummenigge promises, between Bayern, Musiala, who is under contract until 2030, and his representatives to try to find a solution. “We prefer to wait and observe how the situation develops in the coming weeks. We will then have to carefully monitor events before making a decision.» Asked about these statements after last night’s draw, Vincent Kompany preferred to kick into touch. “If Jamal regains his level and form, and if we achieve it together, FC Bayern will come out on top.»

#1391. Can you name every player to score 5+ Premier League goals for Brentford?

Brentford are now into their sixth successive season in the Premier League, and in that short time they’ve boasted some great goalscorers.

#1389. The top 10 goalscorers in Europe in 2026-27: Raphinha, Mbappe, Yamal…

Big names like Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappe and Raphinha are leading the scoring charts across Europe so far this season, but there are also some under-the-radar names and even a golden oldie.

Harry Kane was the top scorer in Europe last season with 36 Bundesliga goals, but he surprisingly doesn’t (yet) feature in the top 10 so far this season.

Here are the top 10 goalscorers from Europe’s five major leagues (Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga and Ligue 1) this season.

Note: if two players are tied on goals, we’ve ordered them by their minutes-per-goal ratio.

Arguably the most Euro 2020-coded footballer of them all, Schick has retired from international football now but is still banging them in for Bayer Leverkusen.

The 30-year-old Czech striker has scored nine goals in 10 Bundesliga games, including in their 4-0 thrashing of Paderborn last time out.

Nobody expected Paris FC to be sitting second in Ligue 1 after 11 rounds of fixtures, but Liam Rosenior is doing a remarkable job in the French capital.

Sinayoko has been central to their unlikely rise. The Mali international scored the winner in their 1-0 win over Auxerre, taking his tally to nine goals in 10 appearances.

Haaland is up to nine goals from his 11 outings of the 2026-27 Premier League campaign. Although he’s drawn blanks in defeats to Brighton and Nottingham Forest.

He’s won three Golden Boots in four years since arriving in England and we really can’t see beyond him claiming another this season.

Keep an eye on this lad. Varela is just 21 years old, but he’s already looking like a serious talent at Serie A underdogs Monza, with almost a goal a game in Serie A since his summer move from Benfica.

The Portuguese youngster has been banging in the goals despite his side’s struggles. Surely bigger clubs will be taking notice.

The extraordinary rise continues. Yamal recently declared himself and Mbappe the best two players on the planet, and he might have a point.

Yamal drew a blank in Barca’s first two games of the season, but hit braces in three consecutive games: against Rayo Vallecano, Valencia and Levante.

He’s now reached double figures in La Liga after just 11 appearances, putting him well on course to surpass his previous best goalscoring campaign.

And with nine assists to go alongside those 10 goals, the teenager is doing a pretty good impression of a prime Lionel Messi.

The West Ham striker curse strikes again.

Fullkrug looked a shadow of his former self during his miserable spell in East London, but he’s rediscovered his goalscoring touch back in Germany.

Still technically a West Ham player, the veteran striker has scored 10 goals in 10 Bundesliga appearances since returning to Werder Bremen.

He’s averaging a goal every 83 minutes, a phenomenal return for a player who looked completely finished in the Premier League.

With Harry Kane out until the new year, and Fullkrug already six goals ahead, it’s not unthinkable that the Werder Bremen man beats the Ballon d’Or holder to the Bundesliga Golden Boot. Who saw that coming?

After signing Zabiri in February but seeing him fail to score in his first six games for the club, Rennes sent him on loan to La Liga newcomers Racing Santander for the 2026-27 season.

He’s hit the ground running with nine goals this year, after coming on as a sub in the first two games of the season.

A hat-trick on his first start against Elche justified the decision to include him and he soon added a match-winning brace against Alaves.

We can safely assume that he won’t be with Racing next season. We wouldn’t be surprised if Rennes cash in, because big-money offers are sure to arrive if he keeps this up.

Malen has been in outstanding form for Roma, scoring 12 goals in just 742 minutes of Serie A football.

The Dutchman is averaging a goal every 61 minutes in the league and also bagged a brace against Real Madrid in the Champions League (albeit in a defeat).

The one-time Aston Villa man is the latest in a long line of strikers to thrive under Gian Piero Gasperini, who has been getting the best out of forwards since Diego Milito at Genoa and later worked wonders with the likes of Duvan Zapata, Luis Muriel and Mateo Retegui at Atalanta.

After finishing runner-up to Harry Kane in the 2026 Ballon d’Or voting, Mbappe is on a mission to make damn sure he gets his hands on the golden ball in 2027.

He has 13 goals from 12 games so far this La Liga season – and he’s only actually needed a handful of those games to get the goals in question.

Mbappe got up and running for the season with a hat-trick against Real Sociedad and has also hit braces against Rayo Vallecano, Sevilla and Barcelona in El Clasico.

Raphinha has been transformed into a striker this season, and it’s working wonders for Barcelona.

The Brazilian has scored an astonishing 15 goals in just 11 La Liga appearances, putting him comfortably clear at the top of Europe’s goalscoring charts.

He’s averaging a goal every 54 minutes, while his three assists underline that he hasn’t completely abandoned his creative instincts. His momentum was stunted slightly with a knee injury suffered while on international duty, but he’s picked up where he left off with three goals in his last three outings.

Barca could have found themselves with a Lewandowski-shaped void up front this season, but Raphinha is having other ideas.

#1387. Premier League ‘expected goals’ tables 2026-27: Arsenal SEVENTH for xG, are Man Utd really relegation bad?

We’re about a quarter of the way through the 2026-27 Premier League season, but the table is beginning to take shape after nine rounds of fixtures. What do the underlying statistics tell us? Which teams are playing better than their results might suggest, and which teams are overperforming?

That’s where good old ‘expected goals’, rattler of Proper Football Men across the country, helps us out. We’ve delved into the data to see which teams are doing best and worst in terms of the quality of chances they’ve created and faced.

Brighton & Hove Albion remain among the division’s most prolific attacking sides, but Manchester City surprisingly remain top of the xG charts. Enzo Maresca’s side have created 21.9xG, just ahead of Brighton’s 21.6xG.

The Seagulls are still comfortably outperforming their underlying numbers, having scored 4.4 goals more than their xG suggests they should have.

Creating bagloads of chances and being clinical with them is a pretty deadly combination – although they finally reverted to the mean a bit in their 2-0 smash-and-grab defeat at Hull City, their 2.51xG the highest output of a team who have failed to score this season.

Elsewhere, there’s plenty for new Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino to mull over when it comes to their underlying numbers.

The Red Devils are fifth for xG, but their defensive record has deteriorated considerably. They rank second-last for the quality of chances they allow the opposition; them boasting the worst defensive record in Europe’s big five leagues is no freak.

Manchester City, Arsenal and Liverpool are all unsurprisingly in the top half. Bournemouth are up in third, while Nottingham Forest and Brighton are also among the division’s top six for chances created.

At the other end, the reigning champions continue to boast comfortably the best defensive numbers in the division. Mikel Arteta’s Gunners have conceded just 9.3xG in 11 matches, 3.2 fewer than second-placed Tottenham.

Arsenal’s ‘expected points’ and xG difference are very healthy as a result, but you’d imagine that Arteta would ideally want them higher than the likes of Manchester United and Nottingham Forest.

Taking a look at the picture as a whole, Carrick’s Manchester United are no longer looking quite so unfortunate. They’ve slipped to 11th for expected goal difference, with a negative xGD of -0.3, and rank 17th for xG against. Their 13 expected points put them 13th in the division.

The underlying numbers are probably most concerning for Crystal Palace, who sit bottom for xG difference (-8.4) and xG against (23.9). That’s a lot of work for Thomas Frank to rectify. Newcastle United are also struggling, ranking 16th for xG difference, while Hull City have created the fewest expected goals in the division.

#1385. Europe’s top 10 dribblers in 2026-27: Brighton loanee leapfrogs Mbappe up to 2nd…

Stars from Barcelona and Real Madrid are currently among those making up the elite of dribblers in Europe’s top five leagues so far.

Here are the 10 players who have completed the most dribbles across Europe’s five major leagues so far (Premier League, La Liga, Ligue 1, Serie A and Bundesliga) this season.

Note: if two players are tied on the number of dribbles completed, we’ve listed them in order of superior success rate.

Soule has been making a habit of featuring in these rankings ever since he first caught the eye as a youngster at Frosinone.

The Argentine has completed 28 dribbles in 12 Serie A appearances this season, successfully beating his man on 59.6% of his 47 attempts.

He’s continuing to deliver the goods at Roma. Still only 23, too.

Doku has completed 29 of his 60 attempted dribbles in the Premier League this season, having played just 487 minutes.

He’s averaging 5.4 successful dribbles per 90 minutes. Nobody in this top 10 comes close to matching that rate. He takes someone on roughly once every eight minutes.

Fresh from becoming the youngest Moroccan player ever to score at a World Cup, Yassine has been playing for Strasbourg.

The BlueCo-owned club have seen Yassine make an impressive start to the campaign, with the youngster continuing to catch the eye in Ligue 1.

Dribbling-wise, he is already up to 30 completed in 11 appearances, having played fewer games than most on this list.

He’s attempted 71 dribbles altogether, with 41 unsuccessful efforts giving him a success rate of 42.3%.

The player has already spoken of how Mourinho has given him the freedom to play where he wants, and so this season is looking a lot more like his first year in Spain when he scored 19 league goals.

His willingness to get forward has also been shown in his dribbling numbers, with Bellingham one of the only midfielders to make the list, having completed 32 in 13 appearances so far.

The England international has attempted 51 dribbles altogether, completing 62.7% of them.

Kvernadze is not a name too many of you will be familiar with, but he is currently proving Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is not the only Georgian winger to be excited about.

Kvernadze plays for Serie A club Frosinone and leads the division for dribbles completed.

His tally of 32 is better than stars at Inter, Roma and Como. The fact he is doing this for little old Frosinone makes it all the more impressive.

Having come through the Malaga youth academy, Larrubia has established himself in the first team of his boyhood club.

Playing on the right wing, he’s made over 140 appearances for the club at the age of 24 and is now the starting choice for Juan Francisco Funes.

This season, he’s attempted 81 dribbles and completed 33 of them, giving him a pretty sketchy success rate of 40.7%. He’s now fifth in Europe’s major leagues for successful dribbles, but no player has registered more unsuccessful attempts than his 48.

Considering he is one of the quickest but also most technically gifted players in the world, it should come as little surprise that Mbappe is among the top three on this list.

His success rate was dented by Madrid’s shock 1-0 loss at Real Betis and 2-1 defeat at Atletico Madrid, but the overall picture is altogether rosier.

He’s attempted 76 dribbles altogether, completing 48.7%. That’s a considerable improvement on his final ranking of sixth last season, which would suggest a change in how Mourinho wants him to play compared to how he did under Xabi Alonso and Alvaro Arbeloa.

Madrid spent big on the 20-year-old winger this summer and they’ll be hoping he can continue to inject some pace and danger into their attack.

Most impressively, he’s only notched 22 unsuccessful dribbles from 60 attempted, giving him a success rate of 63.3%.

Vinicius Junior will have his work cut out to make it back into Jose Mourinho’s preferred XI, and with regular starts Diomande could soon find himself challenging for the top spot on this list.

The Germany international is catching the eye once again at RB Leipzig, having rejoined the Bundesliga club on another loan from Brighton.

Gruda has completed 43 dribbles in just eight league appearances, playing only 523 minutes. That’s an average of one successful dribble every 12 minutes.

He’s also been remarkably efficient, completing 68.3% of his 63 attempted dribbles. You can see why Jurgen Klopp is such a fan.

Barcelona’s teenage wonderkid is leading the list, having completed a ridiculous 53 dribbles in his 13 games so far this season.

Yamal has attempted a staggering 102 dribbles altogether, comfortably more than any other player in Europe’s five major leagues. He’s successful just over half the time (52%), averaging a completed dribble every 20 minutes.

Yamal was top of last year’s rankings and is on track to do it again. What a player.

#1382. Thomas Tuchel faces fight to win trust of England players

Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

Tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”

Tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and said: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”

One player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

There is no immediate sign that Tuchel is ready to change his approach, as he refused to accept the country were angered by his tactics and substitutions in the Argentina game.

In an attempt to gloss over the nature of England’s missed opportunity in the United States, Tuchel claimed that the bronze-medal victory over France was “one of the nicest experiences ever” for supporters and that he did not lose any sleep over his World Cup squad selection.

Tuchel’s defence of the World Cup campaign also included the revelation that his Football Association bosses had assured the England head coach that his job was safe before the last-16 victory over Mexico.

“I tell you something, like 99.9 per cent of the fans don’t speak about substitutions, tactical twists,” Tuchel said. “They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second half, the energy of the Croatia match, they speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against Congo and where they celebrated.

“This is how it should be, this is what a World Cup is for, to connect with the people and to give them experiences that they will not forget. And this is the feedback that I get.”

Asked if he had received any negative feedback at all since the World Cup, Tuchel answered: “No. Not at all. Do you think that’s necessary? I had some quite bad stuff between Argentina and France. [But] No [not since I’ve been back in England].”

The FA publicly backed Tuchel after the defeat by Argentina, but the German has now revealed that he was privately told his job was safe well before that.

Even if England had lost to Mexico and failed to reach the last eight of the World Cup, Tuchel has claimed he would not have been sacked. He said: “There was a moment, a very special moment, before the Mexico game where we had a talk and my bosses told me ‘we know that anything can happen in a football match, we know that anything can happen in a match in Mexico, in a World Cup match, but don’t worry, we see what’s going on and we want to continue like this’.

“It was a beautiful moment for me as a coach. I felt this kind of freedom to take my choices and to just coach freely, and there was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their mind.”

England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 by winning the bronze-medal game against France in a chaotic match in Miami.

“If you look at the 6-4 against France, people talk about it like it’s one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match,” Tuchel said. “So maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best.”

Tuchel has named his first England squad since the World Cup for four Nations League games against Spain, Czech Republic (home and away) and Croatia. He has recalled Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold to his squad, but insists he has lost no sleep over not taking the pair to the World Cup.

“I was very happy with the [World Cup] squad selection, we put a lot of effort and emphasis into the squad selection,” Tuchel said. “And I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic. I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.

“It feels unfulfilled, but, yeah, that’s how it is. We need to move forward with the decisions in the Argentina game. And sometimes as a coach, you can only win if you win. So now we know the result, and we didn’t win. Of course, I reflect and, of course, I’m very critical of myself. But the question that is also still lingering around is, who knows what would have happened? Who knows if we hadn’t made any substitutions what would have happened? And would we have the same sleepless nights?

“So, there’s not much sense in torturing ourselves, looking back. It’s moving forward, but the team, like I said, did brilliantly. And I will not allow 30 minutes against Argentina to override how we view this World Cup.”

Tuchel had warnings for Palmer and Alexander-Arnold, as he said: “It is one thing to be nominated, by the way, with Cole and getting your ticket back in the squad, but it’s another thing to play and keep your place. It’s about when he comes and he needs to show these kinds of performances.”

On Alexander-Arnold, Tuchel added: “Now it’s time to fight for his place. He always said he’s up for a fight, especially for England. So it’s a need to prove that.”

Tuchel said that Alexander-Arnold has been called up as a right-back, rather than a midfielder. Asked if the Real Madrid player offers enough defensively, he answered by saying: “He has to, he has to. It’s necessary. My conviction is that he will, but he has no choice.”

Tuchel has now finished his broadcast duties. It was quite a strange performance from him. I don’t recall ever seeing him read from notes before. His little joke about his bosses telling him off was awkward and felt rehearsed, and the stuff about 99.9 per cent of England fans talking about Mexico and the second half against Croatia was delusional.

It was also jarring to hear him claim that the FA had basically assured Tuchel that his job was safe straight after England beat Mexico. It was a special night, undoubtedly, but did it really deserve that sort of reaction?

“I wanted to give Jarrad a chance. It was a 51 per cent decision on Jarrad.

“It makes no sense to nominate three, four, five number 10s. It just does not help anyone. We can see the form that Morgan [Gibbs-White] is in.

“The minimum I can do is back my bosses. They have my full support on that.

“I’m grateful that I can talk about football because that’s my little bit of knowledge, not sports politics.”

“That’s the beauty of high-level sport, you can’t always win and it makes you feel alive. Not in a very nice way, still you feel that pain of these high-pressure moments.

“As soon as you enter knockout football, it’s a new level of pressure.”

Tuchel has now claimed that people say the 6-4 against France is “maybe one of their best experiences (watching football) ever”.

Again, not something anyone has said to me. Where is Tuchel finding these people?!

Tuchel on Alexander-Arnold: “He comes as a right back.” Sounds like he agrees with Mourinho that the Real Madrid player is not a midfielder.

Tuchel: “There was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their (the FA’s) mind.”

Tuchel says that 99.9 per cent of fans don’t talk about substitutions. He says they speak about the Mexico game and the Croatia game, their emotions and where they watched the matches.

Sorry, Thomas, that’s not my experience at all. Everyone I speak to says he blew the Argentina game. This sounds a bit deluded. According to Tuchel, I must speak to 0.01 per cent of England fans....

FA technical director John McDermott, who has taken a position at the back of the room to listen, had a little laugh when Tuchel joked that he got told off in his FA review for “my substitutions.”

Tuchel says he felt the “full support from my bosses”.

Warning for Palmer: “It’s one thing to get your ticket back, but it’s another thing to keep it.”

He’s expecting Palmer to step up and show him his Chelsea form.

Tuchel says the direction in sports is always forwards and never backwards. “The target is to win the home Euros, of course.”

Tuchel says his feelings on the World Cup are mixed. He thinks there are very positive things to take from the World Cup, but says it was also unfulfilled. He says it’s important to recognise that England won a bronze medal, but says he acknowledges they did not push it over the line.

He says the downside of having the belief they could go and win it is that it hurts even more that they did not.

Tuchel seems to be referring to notes as he speaks. He keeps looking down at a piece of paper he brought in with him.

“The door is always open through performance, behaviour and commitment.”

“They had a good start to the season. Now it’s a new competition. Some positions have injuries. Palmer has his numbers back and a point to prove. Trent was never non-selectable and comes in as a right back.”

We will be hearing from Tuchel very soon. Lots to discuss but the Palmer and Alexander-Arnold call-ups and his World Cup reflections are at the top of the list.
