#1297. A grant to hand out more grants — and build a research area

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Virginia Gewin is a freelance reporter in Portland, Oregon.

Grants worth up to US$10,000 will fund niche scientific problems.Credit: SimpleImages/Getty

Amid political instability and decreased funding for science worldwide, some non-profit organizations are testing whether and how microgrants — awards of US$10,000 or less — can spur innovation. The latest development comes from the Experiment Foundation, a non-profit science funding organization in Berkeley, California, which has launched the Field Building Accelerator to cultivate ingenuity hubs around specific fields of research using small, rapidly deployed grants.

The initiative will, in early 2027, award at least 50 individuals — called field builders — $70,000 each. The recipients, in turn, will design their own microgrant programme to distribute up to $10,000 to researchers exploring distinct facets of the same niche scientific problem. The grants will be hosted on Experiment.com, an online platform that allows organizations to advertise and fund research projects.

“We want to create a different persona in science — the people who can chart new research territory,” says David Lang, executive director of the Experiment Foundation.

The accelerator programme is open to proposals that broadly target oceans, climate, toxicity, future science and conservation technology, says Lang — reflecting the interests of its funders, including non-profit organizations such as the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation in Palo Alto, California. Prospective field builders must propose a name for the field, define its core questions and challenges, and identify at least eight researchers, laboratories or communities they would consider funding.

Judges will select field builders who they think are best placed to identify overlooked talent, back unproven ideas and bring like-minded researchers together. Ideally, says Lang, they will reflect diverse scientific perspectives, including early-career researchers, science journalists, science-fiction authors and venture capitalists. “There are people that build momentum in scientific fields, but they are different from the ones who are getting big publications or spinning out companies,” he says.

And, in a bid to take chances on unconventional ideas, the judges will not average scores; instead, if any of the two or three judges champions an application, it moves forward.

Although some might baulk at the idea that $10,000 grants are large enough to spur new research disciplines, others say it is time to experiment with new ways to distribute research funding. “If we really want to help to seed challenging, high risk, ‘who knows what will happen’ ideas, then small-scale grants are a good strategy,” says Brian Nosek, executive director of the Center for Open Science, a non-profit organization in Charlottesville, Virginia, that promotes transparent and reproducible science.

In 2025, The Science Foundation in Seattle, Washington, organized public donations to award up to $10,000 to researchers who have a compelling ‘what if’ basic-science proposal in the areas of mathematics, physical sciences and biological sciences. The foundation announced the second round of winners on 12 November.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03689-6

#1296. Frustrated Cole Palmer shares frosty exchange with Joao Pedro after upsetting Chelsea staff member before walking off down the tunnel after 4-1 drubbing by Leeds

Published: 16:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 21 November 2026

Cole Palmer was involved in a frustrated exchange with team-mate Joao Pedro after Chelsea crashed to a 4-1 home defeat against Leeds.

The Blues were beaten by Leeds at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 1999, despite having taken the lead through Emmanuel Emegha's first goal for the club.

Noah Okafor scored twice for Leeds either side of a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty, with Brenden Aaronson adding a fourth in stoppage time.

Palmer, who opted against going around the pitch applauding the remaining fans at full-time, was captured approaching Joao Pedro following the match.

The Chelsea star could be seen covering his mouth while speaking to his team-mate, who had been left to watch from the sidelines as he continues his recovery from injury.

Joao Pedro put his hand on Palmer's shoulder as he responded to his team-mate, with the Brazilian then shrugging his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer went to walk down the tunnel.

Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels

Joao Pedro shrugged his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer headed down the tunnel after their exchange. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso was asked post-match about the exchange, amid a suggestion Joao Pedro and Willie Isa, Chelsea's player support and development officer, had attempted to persuade Palmer to applaud the fans.

‘No, we were disappointed, the fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high,' Alonso responded.

'We feel sorry for them and we need to go through together and to find solutions to that and now, as I said, for sure it’s not the easiest moment.

‘It’s a fragile moment but we need to work together and stick together because there is still such a long way to go.'

Alonso's side have now lost three of their last four Premier League matches, having been beaten at home by rivals Tottenham and falling to defeat at Sunderland prior to the international break.

The Blues have now dropped to eighth in the table, with Alonso's side having won five, drawn one and lost five of their 11 matches to date.

Palmer had begun the season brightly under Alonso by scoring in their opening two fixtures but has only scored one league goal since, netting with a penalty in a 2-0 win over Man United.

Chelsea will look to bounce back when they face struggling Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two matches, before blockbuster clashes with Liverpool and Man City.

#1294. Barcola starts to justify £123m price tag with hat-trick as Liverpool hit LASK for six

There was no grand gesture as Bradley Barcola walked back to the bench, just a high-five from Andoni Iraola and some of Liverpool’s coaching staff.

It was a similar situation as he left the stadium. Hood up, jacket zipped, baseball cap pulled on tightly, he politely turned down all requests to talk in English. “Not good enough,” he said with a smile, but that was the only thing that had not been up to standard.

The giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball. On it were the signatures of Liverpool’s squad, congratulating him on a momentous performance that had arrived right on cue.

If you are going end a barren spell, you do not want to just turn on the taps but burst the dam, and that is precisely what Barcola did on a wild night in Austria. He needed one goal to get his Liverpool career up and running, he ended up scoring three.

Iraola had said he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.

Bradley Barcola's first ever senior hat-trick ⚽️ He's been unplayable 🔥 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/UMhUDmGPo9

“I’m really happy for Bradley, because you were asking me yesterday about him, not making the numbers,” Iraola smiled. “Also Florian [Wirtz], and I think both of them played really, really well. They made a difference. Bradley apart from the hat-trick I thought he was a threat.

“He was always one-on-one, certainly in behind and he helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I am happy for both of them, yes. For their confidence for sure, it’s very good. I think they feel now that we trust them a lot. It’s going to be very good for them.”

Barcola should have had the stage to himself on an evening when Liverpool were so obviously better than LASK in Linz but it will have frustrated Iraola immensely that his team scoring six times was tarnished by three daft goals being given up in the final 25 minutes.

We can look at the late switch off in due course but the only place to begin is with Barcola, who looked ready for business as early as the eighth minute when his first touch was a cushioned back heel, taking possession by crossing one leg behind the other, and how he seized his moment.

Liverpool had already taken the lead when Ronald Araújo rose powerfully to head in a Kostas Tsimikas corner but, two minutes after, the Barcola show began, a confident right-footed shot being swept past Lukas Jungwirth from 10 yards after some good build-up play from Rio Ngumoha and Lewis Koumas.

Araujo rises to score his first goal for Liverpool 🔴 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/W1C4iYd89m

Bradley Barcola gets off the mark for Liverpool with an instinctive finish 🔥 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/5K7YBB7UyG

He put his fingers in his ears as he celebrated, with every outfield player running to engulf him, and it was clear how much Barcola was aware of the requirement to get up and running, especially with Cody Gakpo, Alexander Isak and Dominik Szoboszlai injured.

Liverpool needed Barcola to deliver as much as the player himself needed to prove a little point and there is absolutely nothing wrong with having a cause to light a fire. Like a batsman who has been waiting nervously to get off the mark, soon the France international began playing his shots.

There were cushioned touches, changes of gear and even a stunned pass to Ryan Gravenberch, using his heel, that showed confidence had started surging through him and how obvious that was when Wirtz sent him scampering away in the 37th minute to finish with his left foot.

Partnership building... 👀 Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola link up for Liverpool's third 🔥 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/UJC9VW82Q8

That effectively ended the game as a contest, so it was bizarre how it ended up 6-3. Jeremie Frimpong had made it 4-0 and Robert Ljubicic’s reply in the 65th minute looked nothing more than a consolation before Barcola completed his hat-trick.

A brilliant night should have been glossed by Koumas’s first European goal – he matched Steven Gerrard in becoming just the second player aged 21 and under to assist and score for Liverpool in a Champions League game – but LASK kept pushing and exploited spaces to halve the deficit with a double from Florian Flecker, much to Alisson Becker’s obvious disgust.

Look how much it means to Lewis Koumas to score Liverpool's sixth of the night 🥹 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fLYhslbFGq

But some lapses of concentration won’t detract from this being Barcola’s night. The ambition, however, must now be to do it in the Premier League. Liverpool have invested all that money for him to do it over and over again and it would be quite the thing to repeat the trick at Brentford.

“You never know how he is going to play the next day,” Iraola said. “But it wasn’t a big surprise because we were feeling he was in a good place going into the game. He has to enjoy this.”

21 - Lewis Koumas is the second player aged 21 or younger to both score and assist a goal in a UEFA Champions League match for Liverpool, after Steven Gerrard against Dynamo Kyiv in October 2001 (also 21). Emulating. https://t.co/vmfSEaotQ9

A very entertaining way for Liverpool to make it six points from six in the Champions League. The hardest game they have left is Inter away – a fixture they won last season when badly out of form – so they have a real chance to push for a top-two finish that would mean home second legs in the knockout-stages.

This was a good night for Iraola, who was able to rotate before a tough game at Brentford. A hat-trick for Barcola and a much-improved performance from Wirtz were most welcome, but now they need to show some consistency.

Mac Allister and Gravenberch make hard work of clearing a low LASK cross, but they eventually do so. The home team have finished with a flourish and the scoreline looks more respectable for them.

Liverpool’s substitutes have not had the desired effect. Munoz is now on for Barcola, and Ngumoha has gone down with some cramp. The young wingers is substituted, as well as Nyoni, replaced by Mac Allister and Chambers.

Ngumoha too quick for LASK to handle once again, and he is hacked down at the expense of a free-kick. From there, Liverpool win a corner, which they take short and keep possession. Just trying to restore some order in the game.

The score is now LASK 3 Liverpool 6 if you are struggling to keep score. Liverpool have conceded three since Van Dijk was introduced. This was a very tidy finish from Flecker, guiding a bouncing ball beyond Alisson with the inside of his foot.

With the exception of fixtures against a select band of eight or 10 teams, these Champions League nights are becoming like League Cup ties for the Premier League teams: loads of goals, youngsters impressing and senior players in second gear.

The player who scored against Liverpool in December 2023 in the Europa League has done it again, finding an empty net with a diving header after some more loose Liverpool defending.

Denied twice by the offisde flag, Koumas has now scored his first Champions League goal. LASK were caught in possession in their left-back area, and Frimpong delivered to the unmarked Koumas who swept the ball beneath the goalkeeper Jungwirth.

That is a really well-worked Liverpool goal, with Ngumoha slipping a pass between wing-back and centre-back for the run of Frimpong and his low cross picks out Barcola at the back post for a tap-in.

Here come the Liverpool changes, and they come at centre-back: Araujo and Jacquet off, replaced by Van Dijk and Gomez.

Iraola opting to keep his centre-back options fresh, perhaps with an eye on the aerial bombardment that a trip to Brentford can involve. Araujo has been played at right-back domestically.

Wirtz looking a far more confident player, not that this is the most exacting test, and he tests the goalkeeper with a curling shot towards the far corner. There will be just one minute of added time to play.

What a difference a goal makes. Barcola’s touches and feints and skills are getting a full airing now and rightly so. He looks like he is relaxing and he should be aiming to score himself a hat-trick. Liverpool are miles clear of this team.

This game is a non-contest. Gravenberch lines up another shot from the edge of the box, before Barcola shows some quick feet in the box and his side-footed attempt loops over. The question for Iraola is the extent to which these performances and chances created will translate to Premier League standard.

Ryan Gravenberch so unlucky not to score with a shot across Jungwirth, which struck the inside of the far post and bounced away to safety, before a Wirtz shot deflects behind. Liverpool waltzing through the LASK defence with ease now.

Lewis Koumas thought he had scored a third for Liverpool, but the flag was raised for offside. He was a yard or two off, but it was still a very accomplished finish.

Liverpool just need a goal or two from Wirtz now and the night would be complete. LASK actually made a confident start in the first 20 minutes but conceding from a corner has deflated them.

Alisson is the real leader on this pitch for this team.

Then Wirtz tries another dribble through the middle, but his shot is charged down.

Liverpool struggling to clear their lines from the corner, and Schopf scoops a shot over the bar from the edge of the area.

Nyoni then tries a difficult reverse pass back towards Barcola but overcooks it. Moments before, there was a nice touch from Barcola to bring down a switch of play.

Lewis Koumas looking dangerous again, peeling behind LASK’s defence and rounding the goalkeeper Jungwirth on the corner of the penalty area, but he was forced wide and had to settle for a corner which the goalkeeper claims.

Then LASK pour forward again after a cheap giveaway by Araujo, and the home team win a corner of their own. Lively enough start.

Tsimikas scrambling rather to deal with a cross towards Jorgensen, before Alisson puts Liverpool under pressure with a stray pass, and LASK have a corner. Taken short, and then stood up to the back post but Liverpool clear.

Kostas Tsimikas captains Liverpool tonight, not words I ever expected to type but it is a team short of experience. Liverpool enjoying all of the possession so far, LASK are defending in a 5-2-3 shape, so Liverpool’s full-backs should have some time and space. Gravenberch does well to win a foul in midfield.

The home team play in all red, so Liverpool are in their white away strip. It looks like there is some Liverpool support among the locals/neutrals in the home end.

LASK XI: Jungwirth, Jorgensen, Mbuyamba, Alemao, Andrade, Dibango, Danek, Bogarde, Schopf, Lang, Adeniran

Subs: Schutzenauer, Schillinger, Freckleton, Ljubicic, Kalajdzic, Verhaeghe, Elfadli, Flecker, Kane.

A young Liverpool team has been selected to face Linz – the third youngest, according to Opta, that the club have fielded in the Champions League – and Andoni Iraola is being mindful of players such as Virgil van Dijk and Alexis Mac Allister being overburdened ahead of Saturday’s trip to Brentford.

One novice who certainly deserves his starting spot is Trey Nyoni, the England Under-21 international has impressed in the opportunities he has been given so far this year. Watch out for his calmness on the ball and the efficiency with which he uses it.

He should get more chances in the next 10 days, as it is difficult to see Dominik Szoboszlai being ready at least until the home match against Brighton on Sunday week.

Asked about Liverpool’s youthful team, Iraola said: “For me Trey [Nyoni], [Lewis] Koumas and Rio [Ngumoha] are young players coming in from the academy but they are first team players.

“They are first team players because we trust them, and in our situation, where we have some injuries, and we come from playing three days ago. I think they can play well, and I hope they do well.”

24 - Liverpool's starting XI against LASK has an average age of 24 years and 186 days, their third-youngest ever for a UEFA Champions League game, older only than September 2001 v Borussia Dortmund (24y 136d) and December 2020 v Midtjylland (24y 26d). Knocks. https://t.co/4JeW73N87k

Iraola makes four changes from the defeat by City so in come Frimpong, Tsimikas, Nyoni and Ngumoha.

Liverpool XI: Alisson, Frimpong, Araujo, Jacquet, Tsimikas, Nyoni, Gravenberch, Wirtz, Barcola, Koumas, Ngumoha

Subs: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Gomez, Van Dijk, Kerkez, Mac Allister, Munoz, Chambers, McConnell, Danns, Sonni-Lambie, Lucky

Our team to take on LASK ✊ #UCL https://t.co/8vObg7mgLF

It is early days for Bradley Barcola but is has been an underwhelming start to his Liverpool career. The winger was a rotational player at Paris St-Germain, as he is for France, so Liverpool spending £120m is a gamble on his raw athletic attributes and the hope that he pieces everything together.

As Dominic King writes in this piece: “Barcola had no control over the price that Richard Hughes, Liverpool’s former sporting director, brokered with Paris St-Germain for his release. But something he can control is public perception and, with no goals or assists so far, opinions are starting to form.”

Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” said Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

#1293. AI must be held accountable — value statements won’t protect human dignity

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Cindy Skach is an emeritus professor of law at King’s College London.

There is a striking gap in debates about artificial intelligence. Policy bodies and frontier AI laboratories are borrowing the vocabulary of legal constitutions to guide model development and oversight. However, these statements currently don’t include the institutional safeguards that would make such value commitments work.

In September, the UK Parliament’s Joint Committee on Human Rights published its report on AI regulation. It uses ‘human rights’ more than 100 times in as many pages, but doesn’t discuss which rights should be protected or how. AI firm Anthropic in San Francisco, California, has written a ‘constitution’ for its model Claude. In it, numerous values are listed as the tool’s priorities, including the preservation of user autonomy. Yet some of these values, such as autonomy and well-being, compete with each other, as Anthropic acknowledges. The document does not provide an independent arbiter to adjudicate the conflict, or monitor violations by the AI system.

AI governance requires more than just a declaration. It requires a system of accountability. Specific institutions should constrain the tools’ influence in accordance with specific fundamental values and hold firms accountable to individuals affected by AI transgressions. Lawyers call this constitutionalism.

AI is set to completely transform cybersecurity — here’s how researchers must prepare

AI is set to completely transform cybersecurity — here’s how researchers must prepare

As a scholar of constitutional law, I see parallels between the current debate on AI governance and how national constitutions have been crafted, broken, borrowed and fixed.

Countries’ constitutions have distinct underlying priorities affecting their design. These fall roughly into two historical approaches (C. Skach Int. J. Const. Law 7, 175–181; 2009). One takes liberty as its priority: describing what people are free to do and what the state should not do to interfere. The other focuses on human dignity: noting not what individuals may do, but what cannot be done to them, regardless of the circumstances or whether they have consented to it.

Germany’s post-war constitutionalism demonstrates the latter. Its founding document, or basic law, was designed in 1949 to put dignity first and foremost — as both the highest guiding value and a constitutional right, the violation of which is actionable in court. It established an independent federal constitutional court, which citizens can approach directly, that became operational two years later. The choice of this value and the legal institutions to protect it were a response to the atrocities of the Nazi regime, in which people became instruments of state objectives.

Frontier AI companies and policymakers should seriously consider using these features of German constitutionalism. When dignity as a constitutional right is violated — by an AI-generated deepfake or by a chatbot that treats a distressed user as just another interaction — the people affected could petition the court directly, and the perpetrator could be stopped and held accountable.

We need a new ethics for a world of AI agents

We need a new ethics for a world of AI agents

#1291. Revealed: Just two Man United stars are selected in combined XI with Liverpool by stats boffins as Andoni Iraola's defence dominates... but is the Liverpool boss missing a hidden gem?

Published: 01:43 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 01:45 EST, 22 November 2026

All eyes will be on Manchester United's new head coach Mauricio Pochettino when they take on Liverpool at Anfield this afternoon.

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has freshened up the squad since joining in the summer, including the £123million purchase of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, while blending in young emerging talent. They have made a solid start across all four competitions, knocking Chelsea out of the League Cup on penalties, and they currently sit in fourth place in the Premier League.

United have had a dire start to the season, with only one win in 10 games leading to the axeing of head coach Michael Carrick. Will his replacement be able to save the season and galvanise a group of talented but dispirited players?

So, who from United’s struggling side have done enough to break into Sofascore's combined XI based on their performances throughout the 2026-27 season so far?

Manchester United's new head coach Mauricio Pochettino will face his first test against Liverpool on Sunday

United currently sit at 18th in the Premier League after a disappointing start to the season

Between the sticks is Liverpool’s No 1, who since signing for a record fee in 2018, has established himself as one of the best shot-stoppers in the world.

Rated for his positioning, distribution and consistency, Alisson has an impressive record, especially in one-on-one situations.

The 34-year-old Brazilian goalkeeper has kept four clean sheets in 10 league appearances this season, averaging 2.5 saves per game. He has conceded 10 goals, including a brutal 3-0 loss to Manchester City at Anfield last month.

Alisson was poor in Liverpool's 3-2 defeat by Fenerbahce but responded with a fine display in the Reds' 3-1 win over Crystal Palace when back in league action days later.

At right back is Liverpool’s Ronald Araujo, on loan from Barcelona this season, and there are already cries from Liverpool fans to sign him permanently.

The 27-year-old is a natural centre back, but he has done wonders to ease Liverpool’s problems in the right-back position. Jeremie Frimpong started the season in that position but the Liverpool backline were far too exposed. Araujo has helped Liverpool tighten up defensively.

The Uruguayan defender has featured in all of Liverpool’s league matches so far this season, with his defensive actions helping him contribute inside his own penalty box. He has averaged six clearances per game and has won 30 aerial duels so far this season, behind only Virgil van Dijk in the Liverpool squad.

Ronald Araujo (right) has impressed this season for Liverpool, on loan from Barcelona

Jeremy Jacquet is a young player to watch this season after joining Liverpool this summer.

The 21-year-old has a 95 per cent accurate pass rate, including long balls. He had a standout performance against Fulham early on in the season, winning five aerial duels, five recoveries and making a clearance off the line to keep his team in the game.

Despite playing in France's second division just two seasons ago, Jacquet has fitted seamlessly into Iraola's style of play at Liverpool and there are suggestions he is an upgrade on the man he replaced, fellow France international Ibrahima Konate.

Centre back - Virgil van Dijk (Liverpool)

It is no surprise that Liverpool and Netherlands team captain Virgil van Dijk makes it into the XI.

Known for his strength, leadership, speed and aerial ability, he is the only defender to win the UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award, and finished runner-up for both the Ballon d'Or and Best FIFA Men's Player in 2019.

This season, he has shown his aerial ability with 3.8 duels won in the air (79 per cent) per game and 4.8 total duels won per game.

The team struggled against Manchester City, however. In the game at Anfield that ended their unbeaten run, Van Dijk only made four defensive contributions and picked up a yellow card for a frustrated foul on Rayan Cherki in added time.

Van Dijk's contract expires next summer, and the 35-year-old has a big decision to make.

Is Iraola missing a hidden gem? Tsimikas is very much understudy to Milos Kerkez after acting as a reliable deputy to Andy Robertson.

But across all competitions this season he is statistically rated higher than the man who's ahead of him in the pecking order. Kerkez is rated at 6.67 – so it is tight.

Nicknamed 'Greek Scouser' by Reds fans, Tsimikas has only started five games but has produced three assists with 1.78 key passes and 1.56 accurate crosses.

Manchester United, on the other hand, have struggled to fill this position. They were unable to recruit in the summer, and now rely on Luke Shaw – who has been sidelined with a muscular issue since limping off during their 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur in October – and are adapting with makeshift alternatives.

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk celebrates with the fans after beating Crystal Palace

Centre midfield – Dominik Szoboszlai (Liverpool)

Versatile vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai signed a new five-year contract with Liverpool this summer, and has proven his worth after scoring a stoppage-time penalty to level the score in their first game of the season against Newcastle.

With his ability to go forward and send crosses into the box and drop back to defend, Szoboszlai has been crucial for ball recovery, key passes and creating big chances.

It is a testament to his creative ability, including registering four big chances and one assist in the Premier League this season, that he makes the XI despite being sidelined with a hamstring injury for three games.

However, the Hungary midfielder has received backlash from fans for playing 90 minutes for his country in a 2-0 win against Georgia in the UEFA Nations League despite early withdrawal against Palace, and injury concerns remain ahead of this afternoon's clash.

Centre midfield – Kobbie Mainoo (Manchester United)

Only one of two Manchester United players in this line-up, Kobbie Mainoo deserves recognition for his creative efforts this season, which have earned him the second highest Sofascore rating in this XI.

The 21-year-old England midfielder is known for his high pressing and long balls to create chances up the pitch. He has also registered four shots from outside the box.

He has been through some turbulent times at Old Trafford but Michael Carrick turned to him regularly this season.

A product of Manchester United's youth system and there is plenty of potential, especially with new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s penchant for developing young players. A chance to refresh and discover his best form.

Kobbie Mainoo is one of only two United players to make the combined XI this weekend

Centre midfield – Alexis Mac Allister (Liverpool)

After his public revelation that he nearly left Liverpool, Alexis Mac Allister has been in form and pulling the strings in midfield and played an important role in Liverpool's season so far.

He headed in Liverpool’s second goal in their 3-1 away win over Crystal Palace and his passing and playmaking abilities have been key for their attacking chances this season.

He has scored five goals in 16 appearances across all competitions this season.

Right forward – Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United)

The Portugal forward was named the PFA Players' Player of the Year last season, but he has divided United fans this season.

Inconsistent performances and publicly questioning Carrick's tactics after defeat in Como.

In the 1-1 draw against Spurs at Old Trafford, the skipper did not record his first successful pass until the 23rd minute, and he missed a big chance against Chelsea.

He has bagged four goals and two assists in the Premier League so far, but this is largely owing to his hat-trick against Ipswich, which earned him a perfect 10 Sofascore rating.

United fans will hope he can get back to his old ways under Pochettino.

United fans will be desperate to see Bruno Fernandes find consistent performances again

Centre-forward – Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Liverpool’s star striker, transferred for a British record-breaking fee of £125million last summer, has scored eight goals in 14 games this season, showing just how clinical he can be.

Reds fans are finally seeing the form that earned him the big-money move from Newcastle.

Isak edges out United's Bryan Mbeumo to lead the line in this team. He has a 55.6 per cent big chance conversion, scoring a goal every 113 minutes.

The Dutchman is establishing himself as Liverpool's go-to wideman among Iraola's plethora of options. His rapid pace and direct approach proves a massive threat.

This season his end product has improved, notching three goals and supplying six assists in 12 appearances across all competitions.

He is proving to be a reliable outlet while summer signings Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz continue to settle into life in England.

His stunning long-range strike to equalise against Newcastle United shows just how clinical he can be in front of goal.

He averages 1.9 key passes and one big chance per game, which lands him a spot in this XI.

Sofascore's combined XI for United's huge trip to Liverpool this afternoon

#1290. Blues Beaten By Brighton Under Goodison Sun

Everton saw only their second loss at Goodison Park this season in a narrow 1-0 defeat to Brighton in the WSL on Sunday afternoon.

Coming off the back of a three-game unbeaten streak against a trio of top teams of the division, the Blues struggled to take the edge in Sunday’s showdown with the Seagulls.

In the first ten minutes, Brighton’s aggressive pressing pushed the Blues’ backline and forced an error of miscommunication, giving them an early lead.

The next 80 minutes saw the Toffees battle it out to take back control on home ground, but ultimately, they couldn’t find the back of the opposition’s net.

Head Coach Scott Phelan’s line-up was rotated from the team that took on Manchester United in the Subway Players Cup showdown in midweek with Courtney Brosnan in net, a fresh backline and Ruby Mace and Yuka Momiki starting.

After the early concession, Brosnan was called in to action once more to deny Kiko Seike. The forward latched on to a threaded through ball and stabbed at goal, with the Republic of Ireland international standing her ground to deny the visitors a quick second.

On the other end of the pitch, Noemie Mouchon and Momiki took turns to test the Seagulls’ defence, but neither chances could escape Brighton’s Chiamaka Nnadozie in goal.

That concluded the action for the first 45, with both sides battling to take what felt like an imminent second goal of the match, but neither found the back of the net.

Substitutions for the second half saw Jutta Rantala come on for Mouchon at the break.

Just three minutes after the whistle, Everton forward Ornella Vignola received a narrow cross from Momiki just outside of the box. She sent a powerful strike slightly wide of the goal, much to Brighton’s luck.

The Seagulls retaliated with a furious counter-attack. That was no match for Brosnan’s reflexes that guided striker Seike’s shot onto the post, and away from the back of the net.

The remainder of the second half saw a more dangerous side of the Toffees, with Vignola and Rantala both going one-on-one with Brighton’s defence in the 60th and 66th minute after balls from midfield powerhouse Ruby Mace. Yet despite their best efforts, there was still no goal.

With 68 minutes gone, Phelan looked for fresh legs and took off makeshift winger Maz Pacheco for Hannah Cain.

In the 76th minute, another chance fell to Hikaru Kitagawa. This time, the Japanese defender broke through midfield up the left wing and came head-to-head with Brighton’s defence. But, her efforts came to a close when she was faced with pressure and volleyed the ball sharply over the crossbar.

Immediately afterwards, final changes were made to the team, with Aurora Galli coming on for Hannah Blundell.

The action-packed second half came to a final showdown in the 85th minute. Seike crossed to Marisa Olislagers who was waiting outside the box. The Dutch midfielder pelted the ball towards the Toffees' net, but it was met by Brosnan who in yet another odds-defying save, punched the ball over the crossbar to the Seagulls' despair.

Late offences saw the Toffees win two corners, but the Blues were still unable to penetrate Arturo Ruiz’s goal line in a series of struggles in the box.

The final whistle blew and the game came to an end – the affair decided by the unfortunate own goal inside six minutes.

Everton will next play Arsenal at home in the WSL on Friday 11 December. Until then the squad will break off to play in a series of international friendlies.

#1289. Man City dismantled by PSG in breathless Champions League battle

When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

In what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

City will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

Could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

The data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of new signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

In the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

Erling Haaland gets his second of the night, and the game could be back on 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/sFZ0eT2Egz

It could have been a hat-trick. It could even have been four as Haaland, taking the captain’s armband as Rúben Dias was withdrawn during the interval, clipped the top of the crossbar with a header and then was denied by goalkeeper Matvei Safonov as the striker slid in.

“Even with 3-0 in the first half, with the amount of chances we created in the second half, we deserved more. Luis [Enrique, PSG’s coach] said at the end of the game that they were quite lucky,” Maresca claimed before being asked whether he would relish facing PSG again, later in this competition. “My feeling is we are there. We are close,” he added.

Did City deserve a draw? No one was predicting that at half-time as they were suffering as comprehensive a defeat as was inflicted by the commission. Accused of “sham” contracts to inflate income, this was a sham of a performance, made all the more emphatic because of how brilliant PSG, and their exceptional 21-year-old winger Désiré Doué, were.

Désiré Doué with a brilliant finish from range to give PSG an early lead in Manchester 😮‍💨 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/Uwilx7I37H

There is a certain irony that it was PSG who inflicted this defeat, ending City’s run of eight wins from eight in all competitions under Maresca.

It was a meeting of two clubs empowered more than any other by the riches of Gulf states: Abu Dhabi versus Qatar. Both have also had their run-ins over money. Both were sanctioned, but escaped full bans by Uefa for breaching financial fair play rules.

The question, also, was: would the eighth meeting of these clubs in the Champions League in the last 11 seasons be the last for some time?

So we should savour it and we did. That included Pep Guardiola on his first return to the Etihad – in a sign of solidarity – after quitting at the end of last season. Not that he savoured much of what he saw as PSG dominated City to such an extent that their fans adopted the “Poznan” celebration and the home supporters were silenced.

City could have gone in front before they conceded with the erratic Safonov – who was Gianluigi Donnarumma’s understudy and has become his unlikely replacement – punching a corner against his own crossbar before Antoine Semenyo shot the rebound over.

Then PSG ran all over City. They broke far too easily and scored far too easily. Not once, but twice, to go 2-0 up.

For the first, PSG countered, with City struggling to cover, and Doué caught out Donnarumma with a low shot inside his right-hand post from 22 yards.

Then PSG sliced through City’s defence with Ousmane Dembélé scooping the ball across the area to Doué who returned it back. Dembélé stooped to head home.

Finally the City fans found their voices but then they were silenced. What a calamity for Donnarumma as he got a hand to Akliouche’s shot on the turn, but only palmed the ball up in the air before it bounced into the net.

When Manchester City endured their first major sanction over financial fair play in 2014, the biggest club accused alongside them that summer were Paris St-Germain, another Champions League arriviste who had been raised from mediocrity to the elite by some frantic spending from a Middle East fossil fuel dynasty.

Then, 12 years ago, both sides bitterly opposed the Uefa sanctions imposed on them – although they eventually agreed to the terms. Now, they face one another in Manchester with PSG aiming for a third consecutive Champions League title, and City fighting for their lives in the face of an overwhelming guilty verdict for nine years of Premier League rule-breaking.

Both clubs are transformed from the entities that their current owners acquired. While PSG now find themselves at the centre of the new order in European football, City are once again on the outside.

Whatever the outcome of this process, I won’t forget the connection and relationships I had here. It will never be erased.

Good evening, and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Manchester City and Paris St-Germain, champions in 2025 and 2026 and favourites to become only the fourth club, after Real Madrid (who have done it twice), Ajax and Bayern Munich to win a hat-trick of European Cups.

After Manchester City’s conviction by an independent commission on 114 charges of financial malpractice in contravention of Premier League rules, finding the right tone to use to cover their matches during their appeal is difficult. While they are in limbo, the rest of English football is in purgatory and although Gary Neville, the Pope of Pilsworth, in unsurprisingly hyperbolic fashion has said he would prefer not to cover City’s games in future, that is not an indulgence a serious news organisation would countenance. They have to be covered and the issues addressed.

Having said that, in this format of a rolling report on the old minute-by-minute template, I think we have to cover the controversy and its implications in the whole during the build-up and keep an eye on reaction and references to it during the run of play. But I don’t think it would serve anyone to take the stance during the live coverage that anything that is happening on the field is unimportant, redundant and ultimately void because of the guilty verdicts, and hence adopt a flippant tone. I propose once the match starts to treat it as a match while not ignoring the context.

Right, let’s get stuck into the Gulf State sovereign wealth fund derby… sorry, imposible to resist.

City, too, started their European campaign with a win, Erling Haaland scoring both goals in the 2-0 victory over Porto at the Dragao and you won’t need me to remind you that they have won all six of their Premier League games to lead Arsenal by three points at the top of the table.

#1288. Are you a budding science sleuth? Take our plagiarism quiz to test your skills

Dorothy Bishop is emeritus professor of developmental neuropsychology at the University of Oxford, UK.

Reworded scientific phrases can thwart publishers’ plagiarism checkers, but, in many cases, the resulting combinations of words only draw more attention from scientific sleuths. Credit: Gregory Dubus/iStock via Getty

These days, I spend a lot of my time looking through published papers that I suspect are fraudulent. It is a gruelling task. But amid the tedium, there is some light relief, thanks to some hilarious phrases used by authors seeking to avoid detection by plagiarism checkers. It’s hard not to smile when ‘breast cancer’ becomes ‘bosom peril’, or a citation for ‘Baker and Logue’ become ‘Pastry Specialist and Logue’.

I retired in 2022 from the University of Oxford, UK, where I worked as a developmental neuropsychologist. I now track down research fraud as part of a community of scientific sleuths. We work together to identify papers that we consider to be problematic in some way, then send the evidence to publishers or post it on PubPeer, a post-publication peer-review platform. Our aim is for the problematic papers to be investigated and, if appropriate, retracted by their publishers. But, often, publishers are slower and more recalcitrant than many sleuths would like them to be.

‘A waste of time for all of us’: caught in the crossfire of the peer-review wars

‘A waste of time for all of us’: caught in the crossfire of the peer-review wars

Many people blame academia’s ‘publish or perish’ research culture for the rise in problematic papers. Without a large number of publications and citations, prospects for employment, promotion and glittering prizes evaporate. Some researchers cut corners, manipulate or fabricate data, or copy the work of other scientists without citing them.

The demand for desperate researchers to get their name on a publication in any journal has spawned semi-professional organizations known as paper mills. These sell authorship status, with prices that vary depending on the impact factor of the journal. Articles are typically generated using artificial-intelligence tools or plagiarized, and tend to find homes in journals that lack sufficient editorial scrutiny.

One of the few amusing consequences of these developments is the phenomenon of tortured phrases, first described in 2021 by computer scientists Guillaume Cabanac and Cyril Labbé and software engineer Alexander Magazinov1. They analysed huge volumes of research literature to identify patterns. Tortured phrases arise when someone — or, in most cases, a computer — replaces words in a published article with synonyms to evade plagiarism detectors and ultimately publish the result as their own work.

Authorship for sale: Nature investigates how paper mills work

Authorship for sale: Nature investigates how paper mills work

Cabanac and colleagues developed a free website called the Problematic Paper Screener, which documents tortured phrases and other red flags in publications. Detection of tortured phrases has been a communal effort by research sleuths, who document specific articles with tortured phrases on PubPeer.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03040-z

This is an article from the Nature Careers Community, a place for Nature readers to share their professional experiences and advice. Guest posts are encouraged.

#1284. Pierre Sage’s Lyon return ends in disappointment for Crystal Palace

Pierre Sage felt Crystal Palace were “really far off” his expectations after suffering a 3-2 away Europa League defeat by his former side Lyon.

Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half devoid of any shots on target for the visitors.

Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break, before Pavel Sulc restored the two-goal lead, and substitute Daichi Kamada’s late goal proved a mere consolation.

“At the end, we were frustrated by the result, but in the first half we have to be frustrated in the way we play,” said Sage, speaking to PalaceTV.

“I think we didn’t play this first half. We are really far off our standards in the mental side of the play, in the tactical side of the play, because the players are too high between our lines and we really struggled a lot with that.

“When you give back the ball to your opponent, you suffer a lot and we were better in the second half. You cannot win this kind of game by playing only one half.”

Sage’s side got the better of his predecessor, Oliver Glasner, after they bounced back to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 at Selhurst Park on Sunday.

After that victory, the Frenchman called for more consistency from his team, but on Thursday night was left ruing missed opportunities and goals conceded too easily by last season’s Conference League winners.

Sage was sacked by Lyon in January 2025 after a 14-month spell with the Ligue 1 outfit. Like Glasner’s, his own reunion ended in disappointment.

He told Uefa: “It’s a very disappointing return because we lost. I can’t take satisfaction from coming back home or seeing familiar faces when the result isn’t there.

“The scoreline may have been close, but there was a big difference in the way the two teams played.

“We improved considerably after the break and gave ourselves a chance, but conceding that third goal made things difficult.

“I think our second-half efforts deserved an equaliser, although winning would have been a generous reward given that we only really played [to our level] for one half.”

The veteran captain said: “It has been a long time coming. The fans were up for it, the players were up for it so we’re very happy with the performance.”

When asked about Evanilson’s header, which Smith supplied the assist for, he replied: “It wasn’t my best cross but I put it in an area, what a finish from him and I think we deserved that little bit of luck.

“From there on we went on to win the game but in the second half we got a little bit tired but the quality that came off the bench is great and we look forward to Sunday now.

“It’s a great header, he deserved it because he has worked very hard this season and many more to come from him.”

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Thursday night’s European football with Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Bournemouth in Europa League action, and Brighton hosting Kauno Zalgiris in the Uefa Conference League.

Palace manager Pierre Sage managed Lyon between November 2023 and January 2025, and another sub-plot is American businessman John Textor’s involvement with the French club. The former Palace shareholder was the reason the club missed out on Europa League participation last season because Lyon were in the same competition and thus Palace were considered in breach of multi-club ownership rules. Textor sold his stake in Palace, but despite the club’s best efforts they had to settle for the Conference League, a competition they subsequently won.

Palace could have been three or four down against Nottingham Forest at the weekend but fought back for a much-needed Premier League victory. They made a winning start in Europe, beating Lech Poznan 4-0 at Selhurst Park in their opening Europa League game.

Bournemouth and Sunderland also made winning starts, despite both teams’ poor form domestically. Sunderland travel to Portuguese side Torreense, while Sturm Graz are the opposition for Bournemouth’s first ever European game at the Vitality Stadium (or Dean Court if you prefer). Bournemouth continue to be without Justin Kluivert, Eli Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott because of injury.

Brighton are favourites to win the Conference League and play their first game in the competition against Lithuanian club Kauno Zalgiris. Lifting the trophy in Istanbul at the end of the season would assure Brighton of a place in next season’s Europa League, though given their Premier League form and Manchester City’s predicament, Champions League qualification could be a realistic aspiration. Brighton won with 10 men at Sunderland on Saturday, and were successful in their appeal against Pascal Struijk’s red card.

#1283. Cool Palmer has turned into Complaining Cole... his sulking as his club lurches into crisis doesn't say a lot for Chelsea's cultural reset, writes KIERAN GILL

Published: 01:47 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:11 EST, 22 November 2026

We do not know why Cole Palmer headed for the tunnel in a huff after full-time while others in the same Chelsea side paraded the pitch to thank those supporters who had stayed to the end.

Perhaps he was frustrated with himself after a performance in which he did not score, assist, or even test James Trafford in Leeds United’s goal. Maybe he did not fancy thanking those who had been booing as Chelsea trailed 4-1. It is possible he simply does not like losing.

Most superstars can feel the same, and they can show their stroppy side when the game is not going their way.

An extreme example is Bruno Fernandes. Manchester United fans have long accepted his reputation as the Premier League’s temperamental nonpareil because of the numbers he can produce with the whingeing, albeit not so much this season during their downturn.

Such names can get away with petulance when their performances are proper, though Palmer has no such justification currently. The 24-year-old Englishman, unfortunately for Chelsea, put up another anonymous 90 minutes.

We could see he was frustrated even while on the pitch towards the end, with the way he was performatively kicking passes backwards as if to tell everyone else he had no other option. We have seen that before when Chelsea are losing, and it can be somewhat unhelpful when the pressure is being piled on the manager. It indicates the tactical set-up is not to his liking.

Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels

As the biggest name within this Chelsea team and a player whose profile transcends his team-mates’, like it or not, he is the totem when it is all going wrong.

We wax lyrical when he is at his brilliant best. It can be as if there has been an explosion at a praise factory when he is dropping that shoulder to down a helpless defender. We know how terrifically talented he is. He is still compared to that 2023-24 season when his statistics were, in a wonderful way, stupid.

But when he is not performing, so too does he need to take the medicine of disapproval, which came in the form of a chorus of boos aimed at all those in Chelsea shirts at Stamford Bridge.

Leeds had not won at this ground since 1999. They corrected history, then Complaining Cole showed up at full-time.

His reaction did not speak to the cultural reset which Chelsea hoped they had orchestrated in the summer when they finally signed some experience for the changing room, bringing in Danny Welbeck, the 35-year-old whom Palmer has nominated as their new ‘Unc’ after Tosin Adarabioyo’s departure, and Jordan Henderson, 36.

It was a poor show from someone who, in his fourth season at a club that gave him his chance when spending £42.5million to sign him from Manchester City in 2023, should be seen as a leader by now.

Palmer is, probably, still undroppable. Alonso would create an almighty problem for himself if he suddenly relegated his No10 to the substitutes’ bench when playing Nottingham Forest next week. But he is in danger of such conversations cropping up at a time when he should want to be impressing enough to get back into Thomas Tuchel’s England squad at the next opportunity.

We are told both Palmer and Levi Colwill are desperate to represent their country again, but neither are performing to that standard of late. Colwill is a defender devoid of confidence, questioning himself and making mistakes. There was one moment during this demoralising defeat by Leeds when he booted a long ball straight out of play and reprimanded himself for it.

Colwill is perfectly capable of playing a good game. You do not have multiple clubs including Bayern Munich making enquiries with Chelsea without being considered elite. He is in a bad spell, and can come back from it, just like Palmer.

Inevitably, the response of some on social media was to say that Alonso’s time should be up.

For clarity, he is not under threat of suddenly being sacked by those at the top of Chelsea. He is 11 Premier League games into his career, and, clearly, deserves time.

The tactics are on him, absolutely. But he is also dealing with a few issues outside of his control, such as holes in his squad and injuries inflicted, like his highly-influential vice captain Moises Caicedo having to be substituted after 22 minutes in this match.

Xabi Alonso has made errors but was rightly considered a huge coup when Chelsea landed him

When appointed head coach of Bayer Leverkusen in October 2022, they went through patches in the Bundesliga. First, they beat Schalke 4-0, which was good. Then they failed to win any of their next three fixtures, which was bad.

Then they won five in a row – happy days. Then they won only one of their following five – bad days. Then they won five in a row again – perfect. Then they won only one of their next seven – pitiful.

But the following season, Leverkusen won the Bundesliga without losing a single game. Alonso was considered an almighty coup when secured in the summer. A little patience is deserved from my perspective, even if Chelsea are currently in a dismal spell.

It is hard not to think Malo Gusto’s time at Chelsea is almost at an end.

He was priced out of a move in the summer when the club asked for £75million, with Liverpool, Manchester City and others across Europe indicating their interest in that window.

Malo Gusto cut a lonely figure after being beaten for Leeds's fourth goal

But the 23-year-old Frenchman has shown little worth as the season has progressed.

Gusto started in five of Alonso’s first six games in all competitions at the beginning of the campaign.

Since then, he has been handed one start in eight, and that was in the Carabao Cup at Liverpool. Coming on as a substitute in this loss to Leeds, he tried and failed to play Brenden Aaronson offside and was then beaten by his man as the visitors made it 4-1.

We should expect to hear more on Gusto’s situation as January approaches.

#1282. Everton And EDSA Highlights Accessibility Progress At Hill Dickinson Stadium

Everton Football Club and Everton Disabled Supporters’ Association (EDSA) have reaffirmed their commitment to working together to improve the matchday experience for disabled supporters, following their latest quarterly meeting at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

The meeting, held on Wednesday 18 November at Royal Liver Building, provided an opportunity to review the progress made since the Club’s move to its new waterfront home, recognise improvements delivered through supporter feedback and identify further opportunities to enhance accessibility.

EDSA representatives welcomed the Club’s continued engagement and the positive changes introduced across accessible parking, ticketing and matchday services, recognising the value of regular dialogue in helping shape practical improvements.

SIGNIFICANT PROGRESS ON ACCESSIBLE PARKING

Among the most notable improvements has been the significant expansion of accessible parking provision at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Since the beginning of the 2025/26 season, the number of parking spaces available to disabled supporters has increased, placing Everton among the Premier League clubs offering the highest number of accessible parking spaces.

Working closely with EDSA, the Club has also introduced revised traffic management arrangements in the Ten Streets area, helping more Blue Badge holders park closer to the stadium.

The introduction of dedicated parking permits, improved stewarding arrangements and managed access to Nelson Dock has further contributed to a smoother and more organised matchday experience.

EDSA members acknowledged the progress made, with the Club and supporter representatives continuing to work together to address specific traffic management challenges and further improve access.

SUPPORTER FEEDBACK DRIVING TICKETING IMPROVEMENTS

The meeting also highlighted the positive impact of changes to accessibility ticketing, particularly the introduction of an improved resale process for disabled Season Ticket Members.

Originally proposed by EDSA through its discussions with the Club, the process allows accessible seating and wheelchair spaces to be made available to other eligible disabled supporters when Season Ticket Members are unable to attend.

The initiative has provided greater flexibility for supporters, while helping ensure that accessible spaces are utilised wherever possible.

EDSA welcomed the Club’s willingness to involve disabled supporters in developing these processes, recognising the ticket resale initiative as a positive example of how meaningful engagement can translate into practical benefits.

The Club also confirmed that EDSA will continue to be involved in discussions around Season Ticket arrangements for the 2027/28 campaign, with a dedicated meeting planned for January.

CONTINUED INVESTMENT IN MATCHDAY ACCESSIBILITY

Beyond parking and ticketing, a range of additional improvements have been introduced across Hill Dickinson Stadium to enhance comfort, accessibility and independence.

These include the installation of low-level shelving on concourses and cup holders for Personal Assistant seats, alongside the planned introduction of Accessibility Bag Exemption Tags for supporters who need to bring essential medical or accessibility items into the stadium.

A new Access Passport has also been introduced, providing useful stadium information and enabling supporters to share individual accessibility requirements with the Club to help inform the support available to them.

Further measures are being progressed, including the provision of waterproof ponchos for supporters in exposed accessible seating areas during adverse weather.

The quarterly meeting also provided an opportunity for EDSA to raise feedback on the delivery of at-seat food and beverage services, catering options and access arrangements in certain areas of the stadium, including accessibility lift logistics for Club View Members.

The Club has committed to reviewing these matters with the relevant operational teams and catering partner Aramark, ensuring supporter feedback continues to inform improvements.

The continued focus on accessibility comes as Everton prepares to host the launch of the second edition of Level Playing Field’s Accessible Stadia Guide at Hill Dickinson Stadium later this week.

The event will provide another opportunity to highlight the importance of accessibility across football and the role clubs and disabled supporters can play in driving positive change.

Everton and EDSA will continue their regular programme of engagement, with the next quarterly meeting scheduled for February 2027.

Through this ongoing relationship, the Club remains committed to ensuring that feedback from disabled supporters plays a central role in shaping improvements and making Hill Dickinson Stadium a welcoming, accessible and inclusive home for all Evertonians.

#1281. Bruno Fernandes reveals contract negotiations with Manchester United have stalled after he rejected a new deal in the summer

By KATE MCGREAVY, EXECUTIVE SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 04:01 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:10 EST, 22 November 2026

Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Manchester United after he rejected their proposed new deal.

The Manchester United captain's contract is set to expire in June 2027, which means that if the club and player fail to agree fresh terms, Fernandes will be free to discuss a summer move with clubs abroad as early as the January transfer window.

Fernandes has divided United fans during their dire season so far but new manager Mauricio Pochettino confirmed he will remain as captain in his first press conference on Friday.

It was widely known that discussions between Fernandes and Man United began over the summer, on the heels of a strong campaign which saw him named Men's PFA Player of the Year.

But Fernandes has now shed light on his future by admitting contract talks have stalled after the club put a deal on the table.

'No, there's no negotiations ongoing,' Fernandes told Sky Sports ahead of United's trip to Anfield this afternoon. 'But I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years. If I wanted more money I wouldn't be here.

Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Man United

'I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester. Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had a chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

'The thing is I've always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club.

'And I've always said the moment the club thinks is the time for me to move on, I will move on. I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Man United they're going to stay here just by staying, just by finishing my contract and then we will see.

'In the moment the club says "Bruno, it's time to part ways", I'm going to be the first one walking out the door.

'Yeah the club offered me a new contract so I think that from their side shows that they want me to stay.

'As I said there are no negotiations going on. We spoke about the contract at the end of last season. We came in the beginning of the season speaking about the contract but about the context of the team and the club I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, neither for the club to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.'

The club may yet seek to trigger the 12-month extension in Fernandes' contract. Daily Mail Sport understands Galatasaray as well as AC Milan and Saudi are among those monitoring developments.

The Portuguese was linked with a big-money move to Saudi Arabia last year with Al-Hilal reportedly willing to offer a contract worth up to £200m to the midfielder, on top of a £100m transfer fee to United, but he chose to commit his future to the Red Devils.

United currently sit in the relegation zone after a 40-year worst-ever start to the season. Fernandes publicly questioned the former manager's tactics after his side's Champions League thrashing at the hands of Como, and has struggled to find form this season.

Fernandes was brought back into the fold after going through a brief period of being frozen out of Michael Carrick's squad following his incendiary comments following defeat in Italy last month.

Fernandes, who is usually very deliberate in what he says in the media, was scathing in his criticism of coaches after the Como debacle.

'It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball,' he said.

'But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work.'

His post-Como interview was widely condemned by fans and pundits alike, with Gary Neville lamenting: 'If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.'

He also told Fernandes to 'read the room' and accused him of being an 'excuse merchant' on his podcast.

Fernandes was left on the bench for Man United's next Premier League appointment, a loss to Bournemouth, before returning to the starting XI against Chelsea the following matchday.

After Man United's comeback win against Roma, Fernandes was defiant in his post-match remarks as he stressed that he had not been sanctioned for undermining Carrick with his initial interview.

'The club needed that win. The players needed that win. It is something we needed as a group of players and staff,' he said. 'We have been working so hard to get out of this situation together. It has been tough. There has been a lot of speculation in the media.

Mauricio Pochettino confirmed Fernandes will remain as captain in his first press conference

'A lot of lies around many things that have happened at this club, between me and the manager, like that we have cleared the air. Nothing like that happened.

'The manager took a decision of making myself on the bench because I wasn't performing. And that's fair.

'Everyone felt like that was a punishment for the words that I had [after Como]. And if it was, it was right.

'The manager makes the decisions. I have to accept it. I have to go forward with that. It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager, the staff and every player at this club.

'And it doesn't change my aim to win every f***ing game that I have ahead of me.'

Fernandes' comments were ultimately unable to keep Carrick in his job however, with the former club captain finally sacked on November 11 after an agonising three-day wait.

Man United's hierarchy, notably chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, have come under fire from the fanbase and within the club for their treatment of the departing coach, with Carrick taking two days of training at Carrington as they mulled his sacking.

Wilcox and Berrada jetted to Monaco to meet with Ineos chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe and discuss the departure of Carrick, with the club's Glazer ownership ratifying the decision to replace him with United States national team coach Pochettino.

Pochettino swapped the USA for United on Wednesday and will take charge of his first match against bitter rivals Liverpool today.

#1279. Steely Chelsea triumph despite losing Martinez to head injury

This was the afternoon when Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea went from swashbuckling to stoic, thrilling to tenacious.

For all Alonso’s attacking vigour at the start of his reign, there can have been no more symbolically satisfying victory under the new coach than this resolute win at Everton – the most vivid example of an increasingly impressive transformation.

This was what Alonso described as “winning in a different way”. A triumph amid the adversity of losing goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to what appears to be a serious injury after a head collision with Jarrad Branthwaite is just one facet of why the joyous visiting supporters might consider this an early turning point.

Where recently they wilted, on Saturday they thrived in securing a first Premier League clean sheet for nine months.

Much more of this and the adjectives which were splattered across Chelsea during the golden years of José Mourinho – solid, robust and dogged – will be part of the Stamford Bridge lexicon once more.

“Just one day,” Alonso warned, both acclaiming the importance of the win while wisely preaching caution. “It will be key when we manage 10 clean sheets, even though this one feels good. We need to repeat it again and again, but the mentality was very good. Sometimes it is not to play nice, it is to play good – to win second balls, and to be efficient. We needed one of these: a clean sheet and a win.”

Asked about Martinez’s condition, Alonso said: “It was a concussion, but beyond that I do not know. I have only seen one clip of the incident, so we need to wait.

“What we know is that he left the stadium conscious and is now in hospital undergoing precautionary tests.

“We need to wait. Hopefully it will not be too serious, but at the moment we just have to wait.”

Alonso is speedily shifting perceptions of this previously underperforming bunch, the Stamford Bridge culture on and off the pitch already unrecognisable from a few months ago.

It was Chelsea’s trip to Everton last season which facilitated the endgame of Liam Rosenior’s short, but generally hideous reign.

For those who tried to banish memories, it was a darkly comical period when Chelsea’s players were paying their respect to stationary footballs, seemingly finding new ways to stand in front of travelling fans to apologise for meek and rancid performances.

How different the scenes after Pedro Neto’s double on Merseyside – a success built on those old-fashioned and too often underestimated qualities of character and application before the artists had the final say. These are the wins that build connections and trust between players and supporters, especially during the getting-to-know-you period of a managerial tenure. While neutrals mutter about a generally disappointing spectacle, the players and supporters return home clutching three points believing they have fought together in the trenches.

It cannot be overlooked how this win owed a debt to the erratic refereeing of Paul Tierney, especially the amnesty he offered to Morgan Rogers on the stroke of half-time.

Already booked, Rogers was fortunate not to receive a second caution for a lunge on James Garner which took the man after the ball. A replica challenge by Everton’s Harrison Armstrong had warranted a yellow card in Tierney’s world just 21 minutes earlier.

The home team’s argument that this was a potential game changer was supported when the England midfielder was inevitably involved in the move which led to Neto breaking through 44 seconds into the second half – a lead Chelsea never looked like surrendering as Everton’s attacking limitations were exposed.

That should not disguise how this is a different Chelsea, contrasting not just with the characterless and rudderless team of last season, but also the defensively flawed version that began this one. Mike Penders deputised for the stricken Martínez – conscious but taken to hospital as a precaution – and was well-protected.

As much as Alonso’s artistry as a midfield maestro is presumed to define him as a coach, one cannot help but believe there are many who underestimate him as a football student. He was never going to return to England clinging to one idea given his previous Premier League experience, and he intuitively knew an away game at Everton was one for foot soldiers.

He signed Jordan Henderson for such a task. Just like his manager, the former Liverpool captain was primed for enemy territory.

Alonso’s anticipation of a fixture in which a battle had to be fought before there was an outbreak of football proved correct, aided by the fussy and generally terrible first-half officiating of Tierney.

Although Moisés Caicedo was denied a goal-of-the-season contender when a vicious 20-yard volley struck the crossbar, the scrappy, stop-start flavour of the occasion initially suited the hosts.

Alonso’s name has not echoed so loudly across the Mersey since he played a few miles down the road from Everton’s new home. After several calamitous appointments, those fans can believe their team are in safe hands again.

A good win for Chelsea at Everton, but above all, let’s hope Martinez is back to full health soon.

Moyes accepted that his side had were not good enough.
